collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Walking through the gardens, a villager thinks of their life as the seasons of Isola and enjoys this one.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: Walking through the gardens, (name1) finds (him/her)self thinking of (his/her) life like the seasons on Isola. A wet green stretch when (he/she) was young, when everything grew too fast and (he/she) couldn't keep up. A long hot stretch in the middle, busy and dusty and full of work. A stormy patch (he/she) would rather not think about too much. And now this: a softer time, like the cool evenings when the rains are just ending, when things are ripening and there's a little time to sit. (He/she) doesn't know how many seasons are left. Nobody does. (He/she) picks a ripe fruit off a low branch, eats it standing up in the evening light, and decides that whatever season this is, it tastes good.
